[████]                                                Rev. 5. March 2021


         And for corporate management, “it” had now become a strategic 
              decision that could not be reversed. I myself had just 
             experienced about 20 years of technological change in the telecom sector, 
            and decided to establish my own consulting company about 
             convergence. The first job was teaching change. 
          And it was also here that I decided to learn more about 
              psychology. One thing was to be a “parrot” of various 
               theories – another was to understand the basics of e.g. 
             behavior and thought processes in different people’s perceptions.

           Besides Graves, Cowan, Bandler and Woodsmall on NLP-
             psychology, one of the first psychologists I was interested
           in was the then Harvard professor David McClelland,
          who, among other things, worked with needs and defined these
           as fundamental prerequisites for change:

                          1.  A person needs to know how to change.
                    2.  To be willing to change.
                     3. And not be prevented from changing.

           It was probably banal, but nevertheless it is a
             prerequisite that one desires change. People want to change,
             if they are set on achieving something – or avoiding something.
           However, there is not necessarily talk of lasting changes.
           People only really change permanently in life-threatening
              situations, what is characterized by “Change or Die!”.

           It was immediately after Abraham Maslow's death (in
              1970the '70s), that Clare W. Graves, who was one of Maslow’s students,
              first publicly stated his own theory about value systems –
             namely, that [values] develop from the existential conditions,
          which people encounter in the process of having to solve
              various fundamental problematics. A solution to
              existential problems triggers an energy in the existing
            system – but then leads to new existential problems.

            Graves meant, in other words, that (adult and mature)
           people go through a series of developmental stages in life,
          which shape their personality and attitude at a given
             point in time.

           When you face problems that you solve, you will also
             develop a new mindset – and find new problems [to solve]. This
             usually happens in a way where previous problems suddenly
            appear irrelevant – or even laughable – but they nevertheless form
               a framework of experience for solving new
             problems at a higher level.

                                                                             2 of 23

[Source page 3]

[████]                                                Rev. 5. March 2021


           People will at different points in their lives operate
         with different value systems – but will fundamentally rest in a
            particular value system, which is the starting point to
             interact with other people. One could also call this
              “archetypes” (as Jung did – and as Meyers &
              Briggs’ type designations do). Graves gives a characterization
               of a high and a low profile, which refer to an external behavior and
           an internal belief (value perception).

            Graves describes these traits in detail but emphasizes that there
             are not ”human types” (cf. e.g. contemporary HR and
            psychometrics) – but ways of thinking and believing.

           When one operates and reacts in a particular value system, it will
             be possible to identify character traits in the
            underlying systems – but not in the higher ones. I.e.,
            people who react from a lower value system will often
             not be able to understand the rationales or logic of higher systems.
          Conversely, people who have developed to a higher
            system often ”criminalize” the lower systems. Many
              conflicts between people are explained by this.

           It is only when people have reached a certain high
            value system, that they are free from this criminalization – and thus
            also capable of consciously interacting with the lower
             systems on that system's terms. Here it is about
               ”letting go” of the compulsive perception that other
           people express in their behavior and values (their
             attitudes, beliefs, convictions, etc.). At this higher level
           people can interact with others without
           judgmental, emotional interpretation. However, it is also here one
           can talk about manipulation on a higher level.

         So what is Graves’ description of people's behavior and
           their inner beliefs and values?

              I have previously given the ultra-short model description – so here
              follows the more detailed one, where I am faithful to Graves’
             original hierarchical model with a description of
            the value systems from our original consciousness to today's
              various representations.

         And since my original version was in English, here it is for
              the first time in Danish, where I have also updated various
             examples. It is important once again to
             underline that the value systems should not be seen as a
            competition – i.e., it is neither better nor
              worse to be in certain numbered systems.

                                                                             3 of 23

[Source page 4]

[████]                                                Rev. 5. March 2021


           It is also not an IQ system, so intelligence has no
            significance in the different representations – cf. my previous
           chart in the first chapter on learning, motivation, etc. [Which is
             inserted last in the document, editor's note.]

          The first value system is reactive, automatic and about
        survival, expressing oneself unconsciously here-and-now – much like
         the animal survival instinct.


         The high profile is: passivity towards surroundings,
           minimal strength and effort regarding self-preservation.

         The low profile is: minimal awareness of reality,
              indifferent to life and death, helpless.


            This system equals Maslow’s most existential level.
         Think of the movie “Clan of the Cave Bear” – and this
            mindset can really be found in a modern version among e.g.
           street people and prostitutes in slum neighborhoods around the
              world’s big cities. It is the individual who faces life’s inevitable
               dangers. Focus is in the present – and is only about survival.

           The world around them is a direct representation of nature
           and other biological beings. Think for example also of
            the Neanderthals in their first existence, when they meet Homo
             Sapiens.

            Their ”goal in life” is immediate gratification – i.e.
              food, shelter, sex, species survival. At this level, the
            thought process is to survive as a reaction to surroundings.
           It is instincts that are key to survival. People in
             this system can quickly and automatically shift focus, but are
            also dependent on a support system and necessary social
             interaction with stronger individuals. The social organisation
              is a group that can cooperate about e.g. hunting, lookout for
             enemies, and reproduction of the species.

          The second value system is expressed in belonging to
          the tribe (today to the family or company group) at
              a level where it is about sacrificing oneself for traditions –
                for example the elders, the boss, the foreman, etc.


          High profile is: loyalty and trustworthiness, finds strength and
            security in a caring chief, wishes to help the family
            – and draws inspiration from hero worship.

           Low profile is: dependent on the chief or shaman, fears
              breaking taboos – and believes unconditionally in rituals and mysticism.

                                                                             4 of 23

[Source page 5]

[████]                                                Rev. 5. March 2021


          The social organisation is the tribe. Think of
             portrayals of Native Americans and e.g. the Australian
             indigenous population – and today of the few rainforest tribes that still
              exist. Here the past matters – but the present still is a
              condition for survival. The world has become a mysterious place full of
           good and evil spirits. Powerful figures, who can interpret signs in
             nature, offer security in the center of the tribe. It is uncertain
        whether there actually exist more undiscovered jungle tribes in our
               time – but if they exist, they would continue to operate in this
            value system.

             The (super)stition in totems, taboos, signs, spirits, and magic are
              existential values defined by the chief and/or shaman
              . Sacred symbols will be defended by all means
             – and all members of the tribe will sacrifice themselves for the chief
            and traditions. At this level, it is about securing
            the tribe's security for survival. It is the chief,
            the shaman (and the elders), who make all decisions. And everyone
              accepts this – and are proud of it. This is absolute
              submission. Communication and exchange of information
              is top-down controlled.

                 Today no written information will be accepted unless
            it is personally signed by "the boss".

            This value system exists in a pure form in our
            modern times, e.g. as various cults with events with
              the purpose of reliving the past – and in the form of superstition. It
              also exists in the military in a modern form, and in sports clubs
            as well as in families where it is strong traditions that express
             the "tribal form". Globally, it is estimated that there are
            around 10 % with a pure mindset at this level.

          The third system shifts to being egocentric and
             exploitative, and is characterized by being very impulsive and
               able to express oneself without consideration for
              others.


          High profile: energetic, spontaneous, colorful, innovative and
             self-driven – willing to break out of traditions – but can
             also be quite assertive.

           Low profile: raw and unpolished, rebellious, extremely self-absorbed and
               selfish – unable to function in social context with
             others – and often self-destructive.


           In American there is a special term for misfits, raw and
               indifferent types. They are called "Rednecks" – and this word has now

                                                                             5 of 23

[Source page 6]

[████]                                                Rev. 5. March 2021


           almost become universal slang. It can very well resemble
              bikers and other gangs that seek self-satisfaction here-
           and-now – and completely without consideration or regard for others.

           It represents a state of chemical, sensory
               impulsivity. Graves’ thesis of "it's all chemistry" – i.e. that there
               are chemical processes in the brain – was however not in the 1960-
             70's quite as well documented as in today's research,
             where all sorts of "happy pills" can be dispensed.

             The perception of the environment and the world is that it is filled with
               hostilities, where honor and respect work – which
               can quickly turn into shame if one is not constantly
               on top of problems with aggression and raw power. They
               are willing to fight for any real or imagined obstruction.

           People at this level want power and immediate
                 satisfaction of their own needs – and it often happens with
              impulsive whims. In the early version it is about
               breaking free from the tribe's and others' authorities' limitations,
               asserting one's own independence – regardless of what everyone else
                feels or thinks about it.

            If you today think of street gangs and virtually all forms of
             drug dealing and e.g. economic fraud, you are on the track.
            This also applies to modern versions of hardcore
              rappers. Seen from outside, they want to appear direct, strong
            and assertive, ready for action and demand respect, without
               feeling shame themselves. They can be amoral and with an attitude that
                "you have the right to everything you can take." And the fact that you
            can do it makes it right.

         As a mindset they trust no one and life really depends on
              yourself. If it is necessary to fight or
                kill to avoid shame, then you do it.

                 In a softer and more nuanced version it is often expressed in
                bragging, claims, and lies – in general all tricks, to be able to
                      exploit and control other people.

             Historically, these are earlier feudal systems – and today
           the few remaining dictatorships. In a modern sense it can
              be found in smaller privately owned personal businesses where
              "the boss" is often referred to as "psychopath" – just as there are
             persons in larger companies who actually need special
               surveillance. The management philosophy called
              Theory X was invented for these kinds of people.

                                                                             6 of 23

[Source page 7]

[████]                                                Rev. 5. March 2021


           It is also typical that they must be motivated directly with a visible
               (often financial) reward that explains "what's in it
               for them personally." It is direct power reward. This
             also applies in modern sports. If anyone thinks
            of American football, ice hockey – and indeed also
             European football, handball, and cycling – then it exists to
               a greater extent than one (despite the premise of team sports)
               would think. Coaches can forget all about logic and
             group considerations.

                 In the high profile it is often expressed in art, where creativity and
             skill to entertain and delight an audience is the
               positive exploitation of the energy and spontaneity. Psychologically
            it can be compared to various stages of childhood
            and upbringing – especially the teenage stages – where the explanation
               for teenagers being "momentarily insane" can be found in that they
              in fact have not developed the biological frontal lobes that
             belong to thinking about consequences. This has among others been
              described by the English brain scientist John Duncan in his book "How
               Intelligence Happens" from 2010.

           It is estimated that around 20 % of the earth's population have
              this mindset as their primary worldview.

          The fourth system is an absolute system – i.e. based on
            truth and the only right belief, making it easy to
               sacrifice oneself for higher powers – e.g. the church and the system's
               guilt.


          High profile: responsibility and stability, strong perception of law and
              order, traditions – supporter of systems and procedures, well
              organized with clear and unambiguous rules.

           Low profile: intolerant, punitive – can be fanatic and
             insensitive – with a tendency to criminalize and
             dehumanize others who disagree with "the system".


           Here we are talking about a value system with clear and unambiguous social
                rules. This level is based on an absolute conformity of
                right-wrong.

           This is where the world's middle class belongs. They make up about 40 %
                of the world's population.

           It is also here that the perception of sacrificing something now, to
            achieve a reward later, arises. And if anyone thinks
               religion, that is completely correct. Aspects of all
            current religions are present in this value system.

                                                                             7 of 23

[Source page 8]

[████]                                                Rev. 5. March 2021


           It is also here that there for the first time arises a sense of
              the future. This system replaced the hunter-gatherer civilization and
              became the start of agricultural and urban societies, which also were
               the beginning of nations and borders – and not least politics.

           It is a deterministic order, which also applies to
             the formal logic of science such as Newton's Laws. The world
               is rational and divided with fixed definitions that cannot
             be changed.

           The most important goal is to adapt to the highest (true) instance,
             whose only goal is to guide humanity to tread
            "the true path." To this end, maintenance of stability and
            hard work of the individual in the present are required, so that one can achieve
              their well-deserved reward in heaven (and eternity). It should
          therefore also be obvious what happens if you do not
              follow the rules – and it does not await a punishment in the future.

           Also all other ”-isms” are expressed in this formulation – i.e.
            here there may well be a difference in the absolute leader – but it
              is the theme. The scheme is the same: there is only one true faith. It
            therefore also applies to a number of political ideologies – with
            in other words there is no difference between Catholicism and communism.

           The gods are no longer spirits and signs – but real gods,
          who speak through the most dedicated believers, who then
            build churches and monuments for the gods. The king stands above
                everyone and everything – and is, as it sounds: King by the grace of God. This
            also applies to queens and the king's family. Communication
              is primarily top-down – but begins to take horizontal
           form with the king's delegation of power and territories. Under
             the oversight of the nobility, people mind their work and remain in their
              place.

             Written language arises. Doctrines are formulated and political
            groups begin. Rules of conduct are written down – and
              authority is exercised by the person holding a certain
           office. Laws and rules circulate, but since very few at
            the beginning could read, they were read aloud by the feudal powers
            – and it contained plenty of the words "may and must" for
           peasants and craftsmen.

             Even with Gutenberg and better education it succeeded
            kings, nobility and the church to maintain their position – although
           they had to give the country's citizens the right to organize themselves with
               more rights.

                                                                             8 of 23

[Source page 9]

[████]                                                Rev. 5. March 2021


                 In terms of value systems, people in this system
            are completely different from the earlier ego-centric
             system. The two systems simply do not understand each other,
              which the last couple of thousand years of history have fully proven.

           It may be that everyone wanted the same thing – but they
               definitely wanted it for different reasons, and they realized
             it in different ways. The earlier stipulated 40% are thus
             not expressions of all religions and all forms of government's
             populations – but an expression of the absolute value system's
           ways of thinking. And when many people have remained in
             this mindset, it naturally relates to
            the security and stability as a form of reward.

          The fifth system deals with the materialistic – and is
             typically a business form of expression primarily to achieve ”something-
              for-something”, where the self is expressed calculated (as opposed to
             the more egocentric and impulsive third system).


          High profile: ambitious, constructive, and with a desire for
            better social goals and development of more effective
             organizational models and methods – with respect for others'
             well-being.

           Low profile: eloquent, creative – but primarily with ambition
        to achieve results for their own gain (before possibly fulfilling
               goals and values for others) – willing to do anything for “a
               price” – including being willing to cheat and deceive.


           This is where your grandmother is for sale. And it is here in the low
           end of the value system's representation and expression form that
            swindlers and fantasists belong. If you think of, for example, Stein
            Bagger it is spot on. There are also examples like the movie
            ”Wall Street” and the real persons in the world's previous and
             latest economic crises. It is also the characterization of
           the perfect capitalist and the ultimate materialist, who thus
           can be found at both the high and the low level.

                 In the positive expression form, it happens without arousing unnecessary
            envy in others. All energy is directed towards self-expression –
           and the reward must (in contrast to the previous absolute
            value system) come immediately. No reward in
               the afterlife is worth anything. The materialist also believes that he
               or she can manipulate the “system,” so that the reward cannot
             later be demanded back. There is a clear unholy alliance
           between the banks’ rigid rules and individuals who still
              are able to circumvent the rules.

                                                                             9 of 23

[Source page 10]

[████]                                                Rev. 5. March 2021


             The basic idea in this system is that the planet is full of
             resources – and it is the creative and scientific
             exploitation that makes it possible to own and enjoy “the good life,”
             if you are a bit smarter than the others. All rules apply – and
           the attained power, popularity, and prestige can furthermore
            be used for more and more. This is where the 1 % super-rich have their
            base and their clubs. And it is here they use
            delegation with extreme salaries to others, to get
             the practical work done. CEO salaries are at a
             level that is not justified by responsibility – but by the ability to
            make the rich even richer.

            The goal is to escape the earlier constricting system, where
             only the absolute believers enjoyed
           the riches. Now you can create the riches yourself – and you don't
             have to pay "tithe to the church" or others you don't believe in.
            Science and technology are the new gods.

            This level creates the industrial society. And they create
             continuously more and more efficient use of
             resources – including the labor from people. They
           gain the power and right to lead and distribute the work – and they
               get little resistance at the start of this era.

           Communication takes place in an active hierarchy – i.e. both
            top-down – and vice versa – and horizontal or in closed
             circuits. Power and decision processes can be both
             bureaucratic and status-oriented.

         But it is still individuals with delegated responsibility and authority
          who make the final decisions. New technology leads to new
           management: show me the numbers – and what is ROI? Theory Y-
              leadership is the new management mantra. This is where
             decentralization starts – and this is where the competition state
            begins. This mindset belongs to entrepreneurs.

        Those who dare to take risks become the most successful. This creates
              creative competition – but it also creates a “screw without
            end” – i.e. growth and earnings are the only mantra. Politics
           and economy become dependent on each other – and today it is
              capital that chooses the political power – even though it
             formally takes place within the framework of the democratically
            adopted legislation.

           It is among other things the “inheritance” from the previous value system – and it is in
             this new value system perfectly okay to bend the rules a little –
         but it also becomes more difficult to distinguish between means and
           ends for the development of society.

                                                                            10 of 23

[Source page 11]

[████]                                                Rev. 5. March 2021


             Rules and laws are regularly revised if it increases productivity
           and earnings, with a pragmatic attitude towards the community. Such
            pragmatism often results in matters coming down to
            taking from others. This is called “prioritizing” and
             is today called realpolitik.

            Delegation of power – i.e., fines and sanctions outside
            the courts – is a new phenomenon introducing
             administrative decisions. Local municipal bodies get
             “city-kings,” who are also willing to cooperate with local
             entrepreneurs in new ways that are not necessarily for the
             national community. Outsourcing and subcontracting
             complicate responsibility. And it exposes politics and business in
             the welfare state, which is fundamentally based on the perception of
               “right-wrong”, but now gets a little twist of flexible
            double standards.

            This mindset is globally represented with 30 %.
         Together with the previous system, these two value systems
               thus constitute 70 % of the world's way “of being in the world”. This applies
           both on a macro level of nations and on a micro level of
            people, that these mindsets are thought.

                 In our present time, it is thus the materialistic and capitalist
             system that together with regular and religious systems,
              shows the state of the world. That condition thus constitutes the environment
           and problems for a very large part of ordinary
            people who are either not strong in faith or successful
           economically. They react to it – and they can do so
            by moving up or down to other value systems. An unsuccessful
               or impossible materialist can solve problems by
             regressing to communities with fixed rules – or they can solve
            problems in another and new way – for example by taking from
             the rights in the egocentric system.

          The sixth system is relativistic and person-oriented, where
             “sacrificing oneself for the group” is about achieving
            consensus, where everyone can get something out of the community – that is
              “something” that is more important than oneself.


          High profile: human-oriented, seeks inner peace in a
               “realistic” worldview and wishes to take social responsibility
         with genuine and warm relationships.

           Low profile: unrealistic and idealistic expectations about
               “being happy”, expressed in unnuanced perceptions of
               feelings, and “forgetting” to deliver results in the real
             world.

                                                                            11 of 23

[Source page 12]

[████]                                                Rev. 5. March 2021


           Here it is about the personal and humanistic level.
            The energy is directed at the group's welfare and the individual is
                 willing to compromise many own feelings so that
               everyone can achieve something. The world has become too technological – and
           human beings have been reduced to labor and objects.

            We must therefore reinvent humanity – i.e. all
           people have a need to be desired as humans –
           and not as consumers and/or slaves of technology and
             the industry's growth. World poverty must be eradicated, racism
              must be eliminated and self-appointed “god-gurus” (CEOs,
              politicians, etc.) must be exposed – so that everyone again can be one big
              family. This can be achieved by being in contact with oneself and
            others' selves. Thus one becomes aware and empathetic
             toward others' feelings – and together we can create a better
            world with (real) social equality, where all people can
             develop the finest in humanity. If this does not happen
             automatically, it is however allowed to use persuasion – i.e. if
            necessary legislation and power, provided later it can
            be presented as a consensus. A new mindset is emerging.

             Peace, Love and Harmony was the 1960-70’s mantra. It was
            here that the first hippies presented the pure ideal in the form
               of the community's best. It was also here the 68’s
            manifested themselves with demonstrations against wars and inequality.
         And it was here many other protest movements arose, which
             later became global “social, democratic and liberal”
              political parties, that also defined the political visions of
            the welfare society's blessings. It succeeded in Europe's
           old western countries – especially in the Nordic countries – but not in the
                     already communist regimes and not in the USA. In the
           old Western Europe it has now, however, become clear that there is a new
             turn on the way with more “no’s” to the EU bureaucrats. There are
            no concrete practical proposals for solving these life and
             value-related problems in the political system (which still
             was/is capital's and business interests) and a new
            movement is on its way.

                 In the personal form, it was especially teachers in the
            education system and people working in the social professions,
            where empathy and feelings could be expressed directly. It was here
         that one could make a visible and personal difference. That now seems
            impossible due to too much political technocracy.

            NGOs emerged with models and solutions that require a
            different mindset of the definition of community – i.e., without thought of
             personal prestige and privileges.

                                                                            12 of 23

[Source page 13]

[████]                                                Rev. 5. March 2021


           Communication in these new groups happens in all directions
            – but must end with consensus. A new management Theory Z
              arises. It is here HR departments see the light of day. They must
            help the “organization” develop the human
            qualities in the same way as the professional qualifications.
           However, this does not prevent owners and decision-makers in the
               previous value system of profit and productivity from “faking” this
           consideration in public communication. As mentioned, they are
              fully able to “keep up appearances” – and not be detected in
             their own agenda. HR is just a new form of business.

           It is also the precursor for social networks – without
              the internet. It will only work according to the intention
         with the rise of social media – and with a new generation,
          which is not afraid of technology. On the contrary, they
           use it actively and achieve results. They become the transition to the
           next system. This mindset perhaps constitutes about 10 % of
            the world's population, and for good reasons they are mostly present in
           the Western world and in the technological world.

            Graves in his time was nowhere near understanding the
             technological development. His description of this value system
             was therefore based on the industrial society's technologies –
            just as his observations of students and their behavior did not
            include, for example, PCs and the internet.

          The first “IT” back then was the companies’ introduction of
           computers and mainframes in connection with the telecommunications industry's
           beginning digitization. When Graves nevertheless could
             extrapolate to yet another new mindset (the next thereafter), it was
             because his model actually worked with the thesis that
           new problems require new ways of thinking. The problems
           he could foresee were that the relativistic system would not
            “save the world” – and that the person-oriented consideration was just
              a new level of the previous systems focusing on “us – and
             sacrificing the self for the group”. Humanity would develop
                     in an upward spiral. Here technology enters the
               picture. Our development history has been a long journey of
             technological inventions. Graves actually understood the
             exponential effect – but could not predict how
              digitization would create “an internet”. He could, however,
             easily imagine a global communication network – and
              that someone would invent it. It just required a more creative
             version of the entrepreneurs in the materialistic system. And
             that is exactly what happened in exploiting the technology.

                                                                            13 of 23

[Source page 14]

[████]                                                Rev. 5. March 2021


          The seventh system therefore shifts again to an ego-oriented
            expression, where being free, independent and
             self-planning is the highest goal (but not at the
            expense of either the environment or other people).


          High profile: flexible and accepting of all changes,
            focus on functionality – and genuinely concerned about “having
              quality as a human being” – but not in the same way as the
               emotional expression of the previous value system – but as an individual.

           Low profile: self-protective towards changes and with a
            tendency to ignore difficulties, letting things “be” and
           avoiding personal engagement in the life conditions of others.


            This is the systemic mindset. It is the first
           programmers and architects of the IT wave who are the first individuals
         with an overall overview of infrastructures (previously reserved
             for the power and bureaucratic decision-makers). It
              is also this group from which concern for the planet's
             future arises.

             These people function at a higher level than all
           the previous ones because with the new technology they obtain a comprehensive
              picture of the interaction between earlier value systems –
           especially the materialists’ exploitation of natural resources.
         And they are occupied with restoring balance. They use all
             their energy and creativity to invent new methods and new
             technologies for a quick solution if the earth is not to
            perish. They are not so concerned with the earlier value system's
             person-related problems. It is the entire existence of
             the planet’s ecosystem, where humans are just one element – and
             not necessarily the most important.

           They are also those who represent the development of the internet – and
             they are the ones who invent new consumer electronics and app
             uses. They do it altruistically with reference to a
            better world that does not misuse natural resources – and
             at the same time ensures cultural diversity and humanity’s
               continued survival as a species. It is also here the first thoughts
        about the union of humans and technology arise in the form of
              “cyborgs.” There is no mysticism and no emotional feelings
              involved. It is simply an interesting challenge – and it can
              be solved with technology. This mindset is about knowledge and
            information as the new and most important resource. With access
                   to all knowledge – and sharing it with anyone who wants and uses
           it – they are able to continue educating themselves. And they do
               so.

                                                                            14 of 23

[Source page 15]

             The result becomes a new interdisciplinary field where

            Graves’ concept

           Let me finish Graves and psychology with a quick
              caricature-characterization of the various value systems’
            mutual coexistence.

           Most of the world therefore consists of 4 and 5’s. 4’s are the
           more conservative and truly believing (also religiously),
           whereas 5’s are more liberal or socialist (depending
               on geographical location). Both 5 and 6 aim to get 4’s to
                move to their respective levels. 3, like 7, thinks that
              politicians are villains and untrustworthy – and since they cannot do
            anything about it, they just ignore them – however 7’s hope that
           they do not fuck things up. 3’s are typically indifferent. On the other hand
              are 2’s politically engaged and often the most loyal party members,
           making them resemble 4’s – but are more conservative and
              of course on the right wing. Each system’s ”type” has it
             more difficult in communication with other systems. 5 does not understand
             2, because there apparently is no materialistic and
           economic ambition. 4, for example, has big problems with 7’s.
                3, 4 and 6 have on the surface the same ”semantics” – but are
               in different value universes. A judge is, for example, often in
           4 or 6 and a criminal is 3 – and if a 3 says ”sorry”, then
                 a 6 would believe it – without realizing that it is just something
             3he says to get off the hook in the moment. It will also happen next
             time. 4, on the other hand, will demand a real and meticulous proof in
               all details – and throw away the key if it leads to a punishment.

            7 is the non-compulsive level and can generally deal
           and communicate with all the underlying levels “in
             their own language” because they operate in a mindset of the
            overall whole. The 7 people quickly decide whether what is being said
              is “interesting” or not – that is, for the 7 person. For the 7 person it must be
              an interesting problem – not small talk.

            Universal values

         You can of course also reject Graves as a universal model.
           The advertising industry and the media, for example, have their own formulas
           on segment divisions. It is practical in order to achieve a better
              result of a dialogue or a communication. They call it
            quite something different from Graves, Meyers-Briggs or Jung's
              Archetypes – but fundamentally they have the same purpose –
             namely, to establish a ”rapport” with others, whether it is for
              to sell a message or a product.

                 In a meta-summary, it can therefore be stated that people are
               different because they think differently and because they want to achieve
            different things. They do so because their brains and external
            environments are different. Different organizations also develop
               differently depending on the function they perform. They
             seek specific people for specific jobs. Thus, there is
            no universal management model that fits all
            companies. And there is no universal political model that
             fits all social constructions.
